Definition: from G2596 and a derivative of G473; to meet against, i.e. arrive at (literally or figuratively):--attain, come.
BiblicalUsage: To arrive is to meet against and come to the end of the journey, and Paul arrived at Rhegium on the way to Rome, and the church is to come to the unity of the faith and the knowledge of the Son of God. Paul pressed on to attain the resurrection of the dead, and the Corinthians are asked whether the word of God came only to them. The word holds the harbour and the goal together: arrival is the point of the voyage.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Christian life is a voyage with a harbour, and the unity of the faith is the shore we are sailing for. I hold that I have not arrived yet, but I know where the journey ends, and that keeps me rowing.
